newsitem.title: POLAND: Bank Handlowy gives Debica "hold" rating.
newsitem.headline: Bank Handlowy gives Debica "hold" rating.

text.p: Investors should hold shares of Polish tyremaker TC Debica SA as its strong domestic market position in passenger and delivery vehicle tyres made it a good long-term buy, Bank Handlowy SA's brokerage unit said.
"We recommend to investors with long-term investment horizons to hold shares of TC Debica and to buy in the case of a price drop," said the report dated September 13 and released on Monday.
Debica shares rose since September 13 to 62 zlotys from 59 zlotys. @
Handlowy said a bad sign for Debica was tough competition from Stomil Olsztyn, majority-owned by Michelin, and from producers from the Far East and Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA).
It said a good sign was that 80 percent of the firm's exports went to highly-developed countries, providing 42 percent of net sales revenue.
Handlowy predicted Debica would lift revenues to 620 million zlotys this year and 777 million next year from 497.3 million zlotys in 1995. @
It said net profit would rise to 41 million zlotys this year from 35.5 million in 1995. It predicted a 55 million zloty net profit in 1997.
Handlowy said that though Debica had a good cash position, strong competition had eroded its first half net profit, which was at 13.2 million zlotys against 21.1 million in the same period last year.

Handlowy also said majority owner Goodyear would help increase investment and thereby productivity, though Debica was dependent on rubber prices and the firm faced strong trade unions and suffered excessive employment and high wages. @
